reasons: Correct classification: Article IV grants the Licensor a unilateral option to extend the 36-month Initial Period by a further seven years with no opt-out, notice window or uplift cap — a vendor-controlled multi-year renewal, which is walk-away territory and clearly fails the fallback (≤60-day notice window, ≤5% uplift), so a deviation finding and redline are warranted.

Redline is valid and reaches the preferred position: successive 12-month renewals only by mutual written agreement plus a lesser-of-CPI-and-3% cap on renewal fee increases; it also aligns Article IV.I with sub-clauses II and III, which already contemplate mutual written extension.

Edit is confined to the single renewal sentence; the termination and payment sentences are untouched, so the advisory changed-character ratio (0.718) reflects replacement of the offending sentence rather than unnecessary rewriting.

The failed 'notice window ≤ 60 days' regex is a false signal here — mutual-agreement renewal has no non-renewal notice window, and the comment offers the 30-day opt-out auto-renewal fallback as an alternative.
Comment is accurate, first-person plural, concise, cites the playbook position and the fallback without lecturing.
